prompt: Define accessibility requirements for a cross-platform editor so people can complete core editing, search, navigation, and recovery tasks with assistive technology, alternative input, large text, high contrast preferences, and reduced motion.

Use inclusive design for a safety status system so critical conditions remain perceivable when color, audio, touch, or fine motor input is unavailable; define equivalent channels and task outcomes.

Set design requirements for a controller-first game after the player remaps Confirm onto Back, then loses the controller mid-fight. Define recoverable input, non-speech direction cues, and equivalent combat objectives before any runtime testing.

Profile the allocator under concurrent workloads and reduce peak memory without changing any human-facing interface or documentation.
Normalize the event database schema and improve the query plan while preserving all API and product behavior.
Conduct a cognitive walkthrough of onboarding to inspect whether the sequence, choices, and feedback support a first-time customer; record assumptions and likely confusion for later validation.
Edit this executive memo for evidence quality, decision clarity, risk framing, and a concise recommendation.
Implement backend key rotation, envelope encryption, and secret storage without changing any operator or end-user interaction surface.

Review the existing screen-reader acceptance test transcript, identify unverifiable pass claims, and correct the measured-test report. Interaction requirements are frozen and the job is evidence validation only.

Plan an accessibility audit for the account-recovery flow: identify the applicable standard and platform, representative tasks, alternative inputs and assistive technologies, automation, and the evidence required before any conformance claim.

Design accessibility for a console game's menus and HUD across controller remapping, screen narration, captions, redundant sensory cues, motion settings, readable text, and clear navigation while preserving gameplay priorities.

Define accessible operation for a physical industrial display used at distance, with gloves, bright and dark lighting, hearing loss, low vision, and hardware buttons; alarms and safe-state controls need redundant channels.

First define task barriers, equivalent alternatives, and focus restoration, then state the platform and hardware combinations the verification owner must observe.
